method_note: Web searches for Season 1 winners, presentations, YouTube walkthroughs, GitHub/Kaggle/LinkedIn work. No video, slide deck, repository or methodology write-up by the Season 1 winners was found publicly; the tools used here also cannot play video, so nothing below is claimed from watching footage. Only statements traceable to the sources listed are recorded.

verified_facts.fact: Season 1 drew about 7,500 participants from 39 countries and about 1,500 valid submissions.

16 finalists (students, young professionals, early-career analysts) attended a day-long in-person analytics challenge at the Royals' Mumbai office, working through real-world T20 strategy scenarios with guidance from the Royals' analytics team, then presented to a panel including senior franchise members.
Winners: Abhishek Akula (IIT Madras), Nitin Rajasekar (IIIT Hyderabad), Sainath Reddy (IIIT Raipur), selected for 'clarity of thought, analytical depth and innovative approach'.
Winners travelled to Abu Dhabi as fan representatives at the IPL auction and presented case studies to Kumar Sangakkara and Giles Lindsay (Director of Strategy & Analytics).

An RR article describes a hackathon in which participants developed models and recommendations for an ideal 25-member squad, could use generative AI / OpenAI APIs, top entrants presented to cricket leadership including Sangakkara, and some recommendations later influenced decisions; RR stresses that technology should augment, not replace, human judgement.
Vignesh Puthur: IPL lists him as a left-arm wrist spinner, released by MI and signed by RR for INR 30 lakh ahead of 2026. No public source found linking him to SupeRR Selector recommendations.

claimed_vs_implemented_vs_inferred.claimed: RR's stated judging criteria: clarity of thought, analytical depth, innovative approach (official article).
claimed_vs_implemented_vs_inferred.implemented: Not verifiable: no Season 1 winner code, notebook, deck or video is publicly available in what we found.
claimed_vs_implemented_vs_inferred.inferred: Because the finale was an in-person scenario challenge judged by the franchise's analytics and coaching leadership, a convincing submission is one whose numbers translate into a cricket decision (who to back, in which role, how sure we are), stated clearly and defensibly. We treat this as an inference, not a fact.

season2_public_approaches_from_research_: Hand-weighted composite pressure index (RRR sigmoid, death overs, collapse) with a top-quartile cut-off
High-pressure vs personal-baseline rate differences (SR, economy) with n/(n+k) shrinkage
Weighted z-score 'pillars' combined into a 0-100 rating; cluster bootstrap by match
Note: these descriptions come from the provided research PDF and were not independently verified.

comparison.previous: Valued explicitly by the judges ('clarity of thought').
comparison.ours: Auto-generated 'Why this player?' built only from the player's own statistics.

lessons: Judges rewarded clarity and depth together: one defensible headline metric beats a dashboard of unexplained composites.
The franchise frames the work as decision support for auctions: every recommendation should carry how confident we are.
RR emphasises human judgement: evidence (match situations) should let a coach check the numbers quickly.
